events.text:
I've solved the level, and the rule checker confirmed it: the full 102-move sequence ends with both heroes on doors.

**Why it isn't simple:** the right door (20,9) can only be reached by stepping on the crystal after it has been sunk at (19,9). The bard can't ride a sunk crystal. I tested this: once standing on it, it can only step back onto land. A crystal at layer 0 crosses the water only by swapping with the wizard, which sends the wizard the other way. A sunk crystal only moves when the bard is on land within 2 cells of it. So the crystal has to cross in stages. Water cell (10,10) is within 2 cells of land on both islands: (8,8) on the left and (12,12) on the right. That makes it the hand-off point.

**The plan:**
1. **Swap the heroes.** The bard walks to (16,9) and the wizard to (6,9). The wizard looks east and swaps with the bard, so the bard is now on the left island.
2. **Bring the crystal to (5,8).** The bard drags it down column 7, then left and down. The bard can only pull it from 2 cells behind, so it can't drop the crystal into the water on the east side directly.
3. **Reposition the crystal with two wizard swaps.** From (17,8) the wizard swaps with the crystal, sending it to the right island. The wizard then walks to (8,8) and swaps again, so the crystal ends up at (8,8).
4. **Sink it and park it at (10,10).** The bard pushes it into the water at (9,8), walks around it, and drags it to (10,10), finishing at (8,8).
5. **Swap the heroes back.** The wizard, at (17,8), swaps with the bard at (8,8). The wizard then walks to the left door at (3,9).
6. **Bridge to the right door.** The bard collects the crystal from (12,12) and drags it around the north of the right island to (19,9). It never stays within 2 cells of it in a way that would pull it the wrong way. The bard then walks across it onto the right door at (20,9).
